clips.text_zh: 又睇聯儲玩嘢。2yr 10yr 30yr 一齊抽 basis points，term premium 講到天花龍鳳。講cut又unprice，廢。prop firm個倉又係輸緊，靠AI續命🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Bonds just ripped higher across the curve. Two-year, ten-year, thirty-year all moving up in basis points. Fed cuts got priced in, then immediately unpriced. Term premium is the buzzword now. /biz/ says this is the trade — going lunatic on rates. Pure macro pain for anyone short duration this week.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ rate watcher ranting about bond yields and term premium

signal.rationale: OP describes yields ripping higher across the curve — implicitly short bonds / long duration risk

clips.text_en_b2: Bonds just ripped higher across the entire yield curve, with two-year, ten-year, and thirty-year treasuries all climbing in basis points simultaneously. Although the Fed had signalled rate cuts and these got priced in, traders immediately unpriced them once the data rolled in. Term premium has become the buzzword on every desk, while /biz/ is going absolutely lunatic on rates trades. Anyone short duration this week is taking pure macro pain, and prop shops are watching their positions bleed out in real time.
clips.text_en_c1: The Treasury complex has undergone a pronounced repricing across the entire curve, with two-year, ten-year, and thirty-year yields all climbing sharply in basis-point terms. What had initially been priced in as dovish Fed cuts was almost immediately unwound once the data soured. The term-premium narrative, which had been doing the rounds on every macro desk, is now being invoked to rationalise the move. /biz/ is treating this as the trade of the week, with participants going aggressively long duration, while anyone short has been absorbing the pain. Pure macro carnage.
clips.text_en_c2: The entire Treasury curve repriced violently within a single session, with two-, ten-, and thirty-year yields vaulting higher in tandem as basis points bled upward with alarming velocity. The much-vaunted probability of imminent Fed cuts had been priced in, then summarily unpriced within hours, leaving term-premium discourse swirling across every macro desk. Speculators on /biz/ declared rates the singular trade of the moment, while anyone short duration absorbed the bruising reversal. Liquidity evaporated, convexity hedges faltered, and the conventional wisdom that disinflation was imminent was quietly discarded. Markets, having momentarily priced in dovish relief, now find themselves confronting the uncomfortable arithmetic that monetary easing, when it finally arrives, may already be obsolete.

clips.text_zh: DOGE部門廢到連penny都殺埋。US Mint本身係唯一賺錢嘅federal branch，依家cut到自己鼻，真係nothing burger。今個admin每個動作都係stunt😑
clips.text_en_b1: Getting rid of the penny was a stupid token effort by Doge to show progress. The US Mint is literally the only profitable branch of government, a cut-off-your-nose-to-spite-your-face change. /biz/ calls it emblematic of the hare-brained stunts and nothing burgers from this administration. Markets barely react.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ mocking the Doge department's penny removal policy

signal.rationale: Post-hoc political commentary on Doge department, no trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Scrapping the penny was another half-baked token gesture from Doge designed to signal progress rather than deliver any. The US Mint is genuinely the only profitable branch of the federal government, so killing a low-margin coin amounts to cutting off your nose to spite your face. /biz/ sees it as emblematic of the hare-brained stunts and nothing-burger policies this administration keeps churning out. Markets barely reacted, which says everything about how seriously anyone is taking these theatrics.
clips.text_en_c1: The Department of Government Efficiency's decision to discontinue the penny, ostensibly a token cost-saving measure, has been characterised across /biz/ as performative governance at its most cynical. The US Mint, one should note, constitutes the only genuinely profitable branch of the federal government, rendering the move a textbook case of cutting off one's nose to spite one's face. Reaction in the broader market has been negligible, which rather underscores the prevailing view that this administration's interventions amount to little more than headline-grabbing stunts dressed up as substantive reform.
clips.text_en_c2: Doge's latest performative crusade, the abolition of the penny, ostensibly signals fiscal rectitude while betraying an almost theatrical ignorance of institutional economics. The United States Mint remains, rather remarkably, the sole profit-generating branch of the federal apparatus, minting seigniorage revenue that subsidises adjacent operations. To eliminate the denomination is thus the fiscal equivalent of amputating one's own nose, a gesture whose symbolism far exceeds its negligible budgetary contribution. /biz/ commentators have rightly identified it as paradigmatic of an administration whose every initiative oscillates between grandiose stunt and substantive nothingburger. Markets, characteristically indifferent to such political theatre, registered barely a flicker of response, as seasoned observers recognised the gesture for precisely what it was.

clips.text_en_b1: Astra is INSANELY good at manipulating robots to do physical tasks and no one knows why. An anonymous Galaxy General evaluation report shows OpenAI's latest model, GPT-6 Astra, demonstrates remarkable zero-shot generalization in robotic manipulation without any robot-specific fine-tuning. In the RoboDojo benchmark it crushed prior scores.

signal.rationale: AI capability news, no actionable trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Astra is jaw-droppingly good at getting robots to perform physical tasks, and frankly nobody can fully explain why. According to an anonymous Galaxy General evaluation report, OpenAI's latest model GPT-6 Astra shows remarkable zero-shot generalisation in robotic manipulation without any task-specific fine-tuning whatsoever. On the RoboDojo benchmark it absolutely crushed prior scores held by systems like π0.5, suggesting embodied AI has quietly crossed a threshold. While I am still trying to pass my driving licence, the technology is already eyeing my job.
clips.text_en_c1: OpenAI's latest flagship model, GPT-6 Astra, has reportedly achieved results in robotic manipulation that have left the research community genuinely nonplussed. According to an anonymous evaluation document circulating on /g/, the system exhibits striking zero-shot generalisation across physical tasks without any task-specific fine-tuning whatsoever. On the RoboDojo benchmark it demolished prior scores, comfortably outperforming the π0.5 baseline by a considerable margin. If these claims hold, the implications for embodied AI are considerable — particularly for anyone whose career still depends on mastering tasks that machines can now execute on sight.
clips.text_en_c2: Astra, OpenAI's latest flagship, has achieved what seasoned roboticists had previously dismissed as a distant aspiration: zero-shot generalisation across physical manipulation tasks without any task-specific fine-tuning whatsoever. An ostensibly leaked Galaxy General evaluation memorandum indicates that GPT-6 Astra, when interfaced with rudimentary robotic appendages, executes complex physical objectives with proficiency that rivals or surpasses domain-specialised systems. On the notoriously stringent RoboDojo benchmark, performance metrics obliterated prior state-of-the-art scores established by models such as π0.5, prompting considerable disquiet among practitioners whose bespoke pipelines had appeared indispensable. The implications for embodied AI are nothing short of seismic, and even my own modest engineering credentials feel suddenly precarious, given that generalist intelligence has now invaded domains once thought safely artisanal.

clips.text_zh: pol個poster話US係全球最大柴油出口國，Russia已經cut咗，依家US一offline全球on9。印度、中國、亞洲、非洲全部中招。我喺HK都聞到個味😶
clips.text_en_b1: FAMINE INCOMING. US is the world's largest diesel exporter. Russia cut off exports because the hohols kept blowing up their refineries. US goes offline and that is the grand majority of world diesel production gone. Oil Arabia is now just sand Arabia. Affected regions include India, China, all of Asia, Africa, Australia.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ doom post on global diesel supply collapse

signal.rationale: Macro doom post, no specific instrument or levels mentioned

clips.text_en_b2: A poster on /pol/ argues that a global diesel famine is essentially baked in at this point. The United States happens to be the world's largest diesel exporter, while Russia has already cut off exports after Ukrainian strikes kept hammering its refineries. Should the US go offline for any reason, the grand majority of global diesel supply simply vanishes overnight, reducing Saudi Arabia to little more than sand Arabia. India, China, the rest of Asia, Africa and Australia would all feel the squeeze almost immediately.
clips.text_en_c1: With Russia having curtailed diesel exports following sustained Ukrainian strikes on its refineries, the United States now stands as the world's preeminent supplier of distillate fuels. Should American refining capacity go offline for any prolonged period, the global implications would be severe, given that the country accounts for the lion's share of seaborne diesel flows. Import-dependent economies across South Asia, East Asia, and the African continent would face acute shortfalls almost overnight. Even peripheral markets would not escape the contagion, as inventories were already drawn down heading into winter.
clips.text_en_c2: A poster on /pol/ articulated what may prove to be an underappreciated geopolitical inflection point: the United States, as the world's preeminent diesel exporter, has shouldered an enormous share of global supply ever since Russian exports were curtailed following successive refinery bombardments. Should American infrastructure falter, whether through domestic disruption, strategic withdrawal, or otherwise, the consequent vacuum would precipitate an unprecedented energy crisis affecting virtually every petroleum-dependent economy. India, China, the entirety of Asia, sub-Saharan Africa, and Australia would confront acute shortages, while the Gulf petro-states, stripped of their premium markets, would be relegated to mere sand economies bereft of strategic leverage. Even here in Hong Kong, the downstream effects on logistics and consumer pricing are already perceptible.

clips.text_zh: 肥仔信應該睇下：屋企淨係得bench同啞鈴都搞得掂。ABA full body 3日week，中間夾cardio。bench、row、squat、nordic curl、dead bug全部hit晒。羨慕有時間train🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Routine review. I lift at home with only a bench and adjustable dumbbells. I do full body 3 days a week, ABA with cardio between workouts and rest on weekends. A day has bench press, DB rows, skull crushers, DB curls, split squats. B day has shoulder press, hammer curls, farmer walks, nordics. Brutal but works.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ home gym full body ABA routine review

signal.rationale: Fitness routine discussion, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: Routine review for anyone stuck training at home. My entire setup consists of a flat bench and a pair of adjustable dumbbells, yet a brutal full-body programme three days a week still does the job. I run an ABA split with cardio slotted between sessions and proper rest on weekends. Day A hits bench press, dumbbell rows, skull crushers, dumbbell curls and split squats, whereas Day B covers overhead press, hammer curls, farmer walks and Nordic curls. It is relentless, but it genuinely works.
clips.text_en_c1: Routine check, since several users requested one. My entire setup consists of a flat bench and a pair of adjustable dumbbells, which is more than sufficient for a balanced programme. I run a full-body ABA split across three sessions per week, with low-intensity cardio slotted between lifting days and complete rest over the weekend. The A-day rotation covers bench press, dumbbell rows, skull crushers, dumbbell curls, and Bulgarian split squats, while the B-day session emphasises overhead press, hammer curls, weighted farmer's walks, and Nordic curls. Stimulus-to-fatigue ratio is admittedly brutal.
clips.text_en_c2: Routine critique solicited, particularly from those accustomed to commercial gym equipment. My domestic setup consists solely of an adjustable bench and a pair of loadable dumbbells, yet yields surprisingly comprehensive stimulus when programmed appropriately. I adhere to a thrice-weekly full-body protocol arranged in an ABA rotation, with cardiovascular conditioning interspersed between sessions and complete rest reserved for weekends. Day A comprises bench press, dumbbell rows, skull crushers, concentration curls, and Bulgarian split squats; Day B substitutes overhead pressing, hammer curls, weighted farmer's walks, and Nordic hamstring curls. The cumulative volume is punishing, admittedly, but progressive overload remains feasible, and the aesthetic dividends, whilst gradual, have proven decidedly worthwhile.

clips.text_zh: seasonal睇到悶，不如翻睇舊嘢。Hellsing、Wolf's Rain、Bleach、Azumanga Daioh全部想re-watch。Demon Slayer同Gundam 00之外都冇新意lol
clips.text_en_b1: 2000s anime thread. Seasonal stuff is fine and all, but it's often fun to go back. What have you been going back to watch? For me lately it's Hellsing, Wolf's Rain, Bleach and Azumanga Daioh. Old art style hits different than the new seasonal slop. Anyone else on a classic rewatch?
clips.text_en_b2: Seasonal line-ups have started feeling a bit stale, so I figured I would dig out some classics instead. There is something about that early-2000s art direction and storytelling pace that modern seasonal slop simply cannot replicate. Personally I have been working through Hellsing, Wolf's Rain, Bleach and Azumanga Daioh, all of which hold up remarkably well. Aside from Demon Slayer and Gundam 00, recent output feels largely derivative. Anyone else deep in a rewatch rabbit hole right now, or just me?
clips.text_en_c1: Seasonal offerings have grown rather stale of late, so I've been dipping back into the catalogue of the early 2000s with considerable enthusiasm. Recent revisits have included Hellsing's operatic vampire carnage, Wolf's Rain's melancholic animation, Bleach's pre-Soul Society arcs, and the comedic charms of Azumanga Daioh. The aesthetic sensibilities of that era, frankly, hold up remarkably well against the overproduced, committee-designed slop dominating current broadcasts. Outside of Demon Slayer and the Gundam 00 sequel, very little in the contemporary pipeline justifies the investment of an evening.
clips.text_en_c2: The current seasonal slate, whilst sporadically competent, has grown increasingly formulaic, prompting a renewed appetite for the animating sensibilities of the preceding decade. Thread participants were invited to enumerate their recent revisitations of vintage serialised television, and the responses coalesced around several canonical works: Hellsing Ultimate, with its operatic vampire mythology rendered in sumptuous production values; Wolf's Rain, melancholic and atmospherically haunting; Bleach, at least through its initial Soul Society arc; and Azumanga Daioh, whose quotidian absurdities remain disarmingly poignant. The prevailing aesthetic of mid-2000s cel animation possesses a tangible textural warmth that contemporary digital productions, despite their technical refinements, seldom replicate. Beyond Demon Slayer and Gundam 00, genuine novelty remains conspicuously absent.

clips.text_en_b1: Canada literally has no voting rights, just giving the entire economy away. France and Germany steal what little Canada does have. Rest of Europe realizes Canada is just another Greece where the economy exists to prop up extreme government welfare spending. Austerity it to death because it will work this time. Then they elect an extremist government that fucks itself further.
clips.text_en_b2: Canada is, frankly, in a dire situation and shows no sign of climbing out. The country effectively has no voting rights of its own and is essentially handing the entire economy over to Washington. Meanwhile France and Germany are busy siphoning off whatever industrial capacity remains, while an EU associate membership would reduce Canada to another Greece, an economy whose sole purpose is propping up ruinous welfare spending.
clips.text_en_c1: Canada's trajectory, if one takes /biz/ at its word, is essentially terminal. The country has effectively conceded its sovereign economic prerogatives to the United States, ceding meaningful voting rights in the process, while France and Germany proceed to extract what little residual value remains. Continental Europe has apparently identified Canada as a convenient proxy for Greece circa 2010, an economy whose principal function is to underwrite ever-expanding welfare commitments. The prescribed remedy, predictably enough, is yet another round of austerity, which will of course succeed this time.
clips.text_en_c2: Canada's predicament has seldom appeared more parlous, with sovereignty so thoroughly attenuated that meaningful voting rights within its putative alliances have become a constitutional fiction. The economy, rather than being cultivated for domestic prosperity, is being systematically ceded, its residual resources extracted by French and German capital with scant reciprocal obligation. /biz/ commentators have drawn unflattering parallels to Greece's protracted subjugation, wherein the productive base exists principally to underwrite extravagant welfare expenditure, after which punitive austerity is prescribed as though repetition might eventually yield different outcomes. A subsequent electoral cycle, predictably, delivers an extremist administration whose demagoguery merely accelerates the underlying decay. Even prospective diversification into mining surveys provides only fleeting consolation.
